title: Dedicated tier pricing sensitivity analysis (v0.6) — unit economics by tier/shape
content:
Last updated: 2025-02-20
Owners: FP&A (Rishi), Pricing/Finance sponsor (Laura)
Purpose: quantify unit economics and pricing sensitivity for Dedicated tiers mapped to hardware shapes. This sheet is used for (a) tier list price recommendations, (b) discount guardrails, (c) exception policy inputs, and (d) Legal review of remedies/credits impact on margin.

IMPORTANT NOTES / LIMITATIONS
- This is a finance sizing model; not a commitment to specific throughput numbers. It assumes the tier thresholds are finalized in the PRD/ADR and uses fleet baselines + safety factors.
- Results are sensitive to utilization (billable hours / provisioned hours). Dedicated tiers intentionally include headroom; “utilization” here is AFTER required headroom.
- Costs reflect blended fleet cost (commit + on-demand + ops overhead). Region availability constraints will change the blend.
- Does not include one-time onboarding/professional services; assumes standard implementation effort.

TAB: Summary (exec view)
Goal margin targets (gross margin on Dedicated contracts):
- Standard: 55% GM target (acceptable floor 50%)
- Performance: 60% GM target (acceptable floor 55%)
- Premium: 65% GM target (acceptable floor 60%)

Recommended packaging primitive (for quoting): monthly price per “Dedicated Deployment” (shape + tier) with included baseline throughput guarantee and defined burst policy. Overages handled as either (a) additional deployment(s), or (b) short-term burst add-on when available.

Key takeaways (as of v0.6)
1) L4 Standard can hit margin at moderate utilization (>=60%) with relatively low list price; risk is support load + customer expectation management (it’s easy to sell the wrong fit).
2) A100 Performance is the cleanest margin/availability sweet spot; discounting beyond ~18% starts to break 55% GM unless utilization is high.
3) H100 Premium margin is strong at list, but supply volatility and required headroom for SLO compliance reduce effective utilization; region restrictions are mandatory to protect GM.
4) Remedies/credits: a 10% monthly service credit for verified SLO miss has manageable margin impact if capped and if misses are rare; uncapped credits are not viable.

TAB: Inputs (editable)
Assumptions (global)
- Billing unit: per month (730 hours)
- Headroom reserved for SLO compliance + maintenance: 15% Standard, 18% Performance, 22% Premium (reduces billable utilization)
- Managed services overhead (SRE/infra amortized): Standard 6% of revenue, Performance 7%, Premium 9%
- Support cost allocation (CS + Support): Standard $900/mo, Performance $1,200/mo, Premium $2,000/mo
- Control plane + observability infra cost allocation: $350/mo per deployment
- Target term length for list pricing: 12-month commit (month-to-month add 12% uplift)
- Expected discount bands:
  - PLG/small Dedicated: 0–10% (rare)
  - Mid-market: 10–18%
  - Enterprise: 15–25% (requires approval)

Fleet cost assumptions (blended, USD)
(These are internal blended costs, not cloud list)
- L4 GPU-hour: $0.85
- A100 80GB GPU-hour: $2.90
- H100 80GB GPU-hour: $4.75
Additional infra adders (per node-hour)
- CPU/RAM/NVMe + base node costs: $0.40 (L4 node), $0.55 (A100 node), $0.75 (H100 node)
- Network (egress + cross-AZ, averaged): $0.08 per GPU-hour equivalent (varies by region)

Base utilization scenarios (post headroom)
- Low: 50%
- Base: 65%
- High: 78%

TAB: Shapes + tier mapping (pricing-relevant shapes only)
NOTE: final supported shapes by tier are tracked in the shapes catalog; below is the subset used for pricing sensitivity.

Shape IDs (finance shorthand)
- L4x4 (single node): 4x L4, no NVLink, optimized for cost
- A100x8 (single node): 8x A100 80GB, NVLink
- H100x8 (single node): 8x H100 80GB, NVLink

Tier to shape allowed (current assumption)
- Standard: L4x4, (A100x8 allowed for customers needing higher context lengths but not Premium features)
- Performance: A100x8 (primary), H100x8 limited availability
- Premium: H100x8 only (region-restricted)

TAB: Unit economics (base case)
Definitions
- Provisioned cost/mo = 730h * (GPU-hour * GPU_count + node_adders * node_count + network_adder * GPU_count)
- Effective billable hours = 730h * utilization
- Revenue/mo = list_price/mo * (1 - discount)
- GM% = (Revenue - Provisioned cost - support - control_plane - managed_overhead) / Revenue

Base case assumes: utilization=65%, discount=15% (enterprise-ish), overhead as per tier.

Table: Base case economics (v0.6)
Columns: Tier | Shape | GPU count | Provisioned cost/mo | Suggested list price/mo | Revenue/mo @15% disc | Est. GM% @65% util

Standard | L4x4 | 4 | $3,290 | $12,500 | $10,625 | 54–58%
Performance | A100x8 | 8 | $19,740 | $58,000 | $49,300 | 56–61%
Premium | H100x8 | 8 | $32,650 | $98,000 | $83,300 | 60–66%

Notes on the ranges above
- GM% range reflects network variance (+/- 20%) and support variance (+/- 25% based on incident rate).
- Premium assumes stricter headroom but we model it in utilization; if headroom increases further due to supply/maintenance constraints, effective utilization falls.

TAB: Sensitivity matrix (what moves margin)
Sensitivity 1: Utilization impact (holding list price constant, discount=15%)

Standard / L4x4 @ list $12.5k
- Util 50%: GM ~ 45–49% (below floor)
- Util 65%: GM ~ 54–58%
- Util 78%: GM ~ 60–63%

Performance / A100x8 @ list $58k
- Util 50%: GM ~ 48–52% (borderline)
- Util 65%: GM ~ 56–61%
- Util 78%: GM ~ 62–66%

Premium / H100x8 @ list $98k
- Util 50%: GM ~ 54–58% (below Premium target, above floor)
- Util 65%: GM ~ 60–66%
- Util 78%: GM ~ 66–70%

Sensitivity 2: Discount impact (holding utilization=65%)

Performance / A100x8 @ list $58k
- 10% discount: GM ~ 59–63%
- 15% discount: GM ~ 56–61%
- 20% discount: GM ~ 53–58%
- 25% discount: GM ~ 49–54% (requires approval + utilization plan)

Premium / H100x8 @ list $98k
- 10% discount: GM ~ 63–68%
- 15% discount: GM ~ 60–66%
- 20% discount: GM ~ 57–63% (still workable with region restrictions)
- 25% discount: GM ~ 53–59% (requires exec approval)

Sensitivity 3: Fleet cost shocks (GPU-hour +/- 15%)

If A100 GPU-hour increases +15% (to $3.34)
- Performance / A100x8 GM drops ~3–4 pts at same price/discount.
Mitigation: tighten discounts, enforce region availability, or increase list by ~6–8%.

If H100 GPU-hour increases +15% (to $5.46)
- Premium / H100x8 GM drops ~4–5 pts.
Mitigation: Premium list +8–10% OR reduce discount cap OR require longer term.

TAB: Optional pricing primitive checks (per throughput vs per shape)
Option A (recommended): Sell deployment shape + tier (monthly). Throughput guarantee is a tier attribute with explicit assumptions.
- Pros: simplest contracts, aligned with fleet procurement, reduces disputes.
- Cons: customers will ask “what tokens/sec am I buying?” — requires strong tier docs + measurement standard.

Option B: Sell guaranteed sustained output tokens/sec (rate card), with shapes abstracted.
- Pros: maps to customer language.
- Cons: creates significant economic risk under prompt distribution shifts; requires real-time enforcement and excludes many workloads; Legal complexity.

Conclusion: stick with Option A for initial launch; revisit tokens/sec-based price metric only if/when measurement standard is stable + enforcement is mature.

TAB: Remedies/credits stress test (Legal input)
Assume contract includes: credit = 10% of monthly fees for impacted deployment for verified SLO breach; cap 20% per month; excludes customer-induced load and scheduled maintenance per measurement standard.

Stress scenarios (annualized margin impact)
- “Good year”: 0.5% of months have a credit event => ~0.05–0.10 pts GM drag (negligible)
- “Noisy year”: 2% of months have a credit event => ~0.2–0.4 pts GM drag
- “Bad year”: 6% of months have a credit event => ~0.7–1.2 pts GM drag + churn risk (this is really an SRE/quality issue; pricing can’t save it)

Notes:
- Uncapped credits (or credits applied to whole contract value) are not viable economically.
- Consider language: credit applies only to the specific Dedicated deployment(s) failing the SLO, not the customer’s entire Redwood footprint.

TAB: Approval review notes (open items / asks)
1) Confirm discount guardrails by tier (proposal)
- Standard: max 15% without Finance approval; max 20% with Finance
- Performance: max 18% without Finance; 25% requires Finance + Product signoff and utilization plan
- Premium: max 15% without Finance; 20% requires Finance; >20% requires Exec sponsor (Evelyn) due to supply risk

2) Region restrictions (must be part of packaging)
- Premium H100x8: limit to regions with predictable supply + maintenance coverage (per Infra). If Sales requests exception, require pricing uplift OR longer term.

3) Add-on policy
- Short-term burst add-on: price as % uplift to monthly fee when capacity is available; do not include in base list assumptions.
- Additional replicas: treated as additional deployments; pro-rate monthly.

4) Contract language alignment
- Ensure measurement standard is referenced by name and version.
- Ensure carve-outs match SRE’s definition (maintenance windows, customer-induced overload, invalid requests).

5) Finance asks to Product/SRE
- Provide expected incident rate for Dedicated tiers post-guardrails (rough order-of-magnitude) to validate support allocation.
- Provide expected headroom requirement per tier as enforcement/admission control ships.

Changelog
- 2025-01-29: v0.1 created (initial cost inputs + rough tier prices)
- 2025-02-07: v0.4 updated with new headroom assumptions + support costs; shared with Product (Lauren)
- 2025-02-20: v0.6 updated with discount sensitivity and remedies stress test for Legal (Michael)
